title: Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust
meta_description: Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust services from Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, platforms and committed outcomes.

blocks.x: Threats contained in minutes, not days — zero-trust architectures with MTTD/MTTR targets, control coverage and audit findings committed per gate.

Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust covers architecture-level security programs: zero-trust network and workload design, identity modernization, threat intelligence and managed detection, cloud posture management, AI-specific security for models and agents, cyber resilience, and the compliance machinery (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, DORA) that regulated industries must evidence. We design for the assumption of breach and the reality of audit.

The attack surface grew faster than the org chart: SaaS sprawl, machine identities outnumbering human ones, and AI systems that can be poisoned or prompted into leakage. Frameworks hardened in response — NIST CSF 2.0, DORA in the EU, SEC disclosure rules in the US — making security a board-level, evidence-first discipline.

items: Never trust, always verify: zero-trust as an executable architecture, not a slide.
Detection that keeps pace: intelligence-driven SOC with the boring parts (tuning, coverage) done properly.
Identity as the perimeter: workforce, customer and machine identities on one governed plane.
Secure at the control plane: posture, workload and data security engineered into the platform.
Secure the models themselves: prompt-injection defense, agent containment and AI red-teaming.
Assume breach, plan recovery: resilience engineered, rehearsed and measured.
Evidence once, audit anywhere: compliance automation across SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, DORA and privacy.

blocks.x: Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass carry the production rails for this tower — governance, security posture and audit evidence production are inherited from the platform, so programs harden instead of improvising.

items: Measured down to near-zero across tiers
Down 40-60% within two quarters of tuning cadence

blocks.x: Anchor industries: Banking & Financial Services, Energy & Utilities, Healthcare & Life Sciences, Insurance & Risk, Manufacturing & Industrial, Public Sector & Government, Retail & Consumer Goods, Technology & SaaS, Telecom, Media & Entertainment.

Every program of this type runs the same weekly rhythm, so your team can plan around it. Weeks 1–2 are measurement only: we lock the current metric with your team and both sides sign it before a line of build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver a bounded pilot — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a named control owner on your side. Weeks 9–12 turn what worked into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, then report the measured delta against the baseline. A missed gate means a documented stop-or-redirect decision, not a quiet extension.
At the end of the first quarter of a typical program you hold four concrete assets:

items: The signed measurement of where the metric stands today, with the method written out so the number can be defended to finance.
Every automated decision path, its policy checks, its human checkpoint and its owner on one page.
Logs, evaluations and approvals collected automatically as the program runs — ready for internal audit or a regulator.
A running record of the delta against baseline, updated at every gate, reviewed at every steering meeting.
